cleanIntro: The Model 3500 is the 3 1/2 inch supermagnum member of Stoeger's inertia line, and it is mechanically the same gun as the Model 3000 with a longer chamber: a rotating locking head with two lugs, an inertia spring trapped behind it, no gas system to foul. What changes with the chamber is the ammunition ceiling and the magazine count -- three 3 1/2 inch, four 3 inch or five 2 3/4 inch. Do not work from the 3000's book; the two are near-identical in every section except the one that matters here.

steps.title: Safety on, bolt back, chamber empty
steps.action: Rest the butt on your hip and draw the bolt handle back; the chambered round is extracted and thrown out of the ejection port. Look and feel inside the chamber -- a 3 1/2 inch hull is long enough to hang on the carrier if the bolt is eased rather than pulled, and a half-fed shell reads as an empty gun from the outside. Then let the bolt close on the empty chamber.
steps.quote: 1. Rest the butt of the stock on your hip and open the bolt by pulling back on the bolt lever. The round in the chamber will be extracted from the chamber and ejected.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — UNLOADING, step 1, p.11
steps.warn: PUT THE MANUAL SAFETY IN THE "ON" OR "SAFE" POSITION.

steps.title: Empty the magazine -- count by shell length
steps.action: Turn the gun over, push the carrier down and press the front of the carrier latch once per shell. How many you are looking for depends on what is in there: the 3500's tube takes three 3 1/2 inch, four 3 inch or five 2 3/4 inch rounds, so the count is not fixed and 'it felt empty' is not a check. Keep pressing the latch until nothing more comes out, then look into the tube.
steps.prose: The magazine spring is at its stiffest with a full tube of long shells; let them come out to you.
steps.caution: CAUTION: The magazine spring, when fully compressed, can yield enough force to cause injury during the unloading process. Use care when unloading the magazine.
steps.quote: The ammunition magazine, depending on the cartridge type, can accommodate three 31/2" rounds, four 3" rounds or five 23/4" rounds.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — LOADING, p.10

steps.title: M3500 chamber ceiling: 12 gauge, 2 3/4 to 3 1/2 inch
steps.action: Confirm the barrel marking before you shoot or judge a malfunction. The Model 3500 is the 3 1/2 inch gun of the pair and will feed everything from a 2 3/4 inch target load up to a 3 1/2 inch supermagnum. That range is what separates it from the Model 3000, whose ceiling is 3 inch -- and because the two manuals share layout and figure numbers, this is the one line you cannot borrow from the other book.
steps.prose: A case longer than the chamber has serious consequences for both the gun and the shooter.
steps.quote: USE ONLY SUITABLE AMMUNITION: This Stoeger semi-automatic shotgun is chambered in 12 gauge. It has been designed to fire 23/4" (70mm) to 3 1/2" (89mm) length with lead or steel shot. Use of Full or Improved Modified choke tubes is not recommended with steel shot.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — AMMUNITION, p.18

steps.title: Magazine cap off, barrel and forend forward off the tube
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap and take it off the tube. Hold the stock/receiver in your right hand, the barrel/forend in your left, and pull the barrel assembly forward off the magazine tube. A slight rotation back and forth eases the barrel out of its seat in the receiver -- that seat is a close fit by design, and dragging it off square is what scores it.
steps.quote: 2. While resting the stock against your hip, grab the stock/receiver assembly with your right hand and the barrel/forend assembly with the left hand. Pull the latter forward and completely off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY, step 2, p.13

steps.title: Forend off the barrel ring
steps.action: Rotate the rear of the forend away from the barrel, then pull it off the barrel ring. It is held on that ring alone, so no tool is needed once the angle is right; pulling straight without rotating first just jams it on the ring.
steps.prose: Barrel and forend now separate into the two pieces the gun ships in.
steps.quote: 3. Rotate the rear of the forend assembly and separate it from the barrel by pulling it off of the barrel ring.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY, step 3, p.13

steps.title: Bolt handle out with the action held slightly open
steps.action: Hold the action open a crack and pull the bolt handle straight out of the bolt. It is a slip fit with no detent to fight, but it only releases at that partly-open position where the handle lines up with its cut. If it resists, move the bolt a few millimetres rather than levering on the handle.
steps.quote: 4. Pull the bolt handle off the bolt while holding the action open slightly.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY, step 4, p.13
steps.warn: WARNING: Visually and manually check the chamber and magazine to be certain the gun is completely unloaded.

steps.title: Ease the bolt forward against the recoil spring, then draw it out
steps.action: Support the action bar with your left hand before touching the carrier release -- the recoil spring rides the magazine tube and is loaded with the bolt back. Press the carrier release and walk the bolt forward under control until the spring goes slack, then pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver. Letting it snap forward instead hammers the bolt face against a chamber it is not locked into.
steps.caution: 6. Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver.
steps.quote: 5. While holding the action bar with your left hand to counterbalance the thrust of the recoil spring, push the carrier release button (Fig. 17) and ease the bolt forward until the recoil spring no longer pushes it forward.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY, step 5, p.14

steps.title: Bore, choke recess, bolt rails and magazine tube
steps.action: Run the bore with the choke tube still in place so fouling and solvent stay off the internal barrel threads, then take the choke out and clean it and its recess on their own. Wipe the receiver clean and oil the bolt rails and the outside of the magazine tube. On a 3 1/2 inch gun the tube sees the heaviest recoil-spring cycling in the line, and grit there shows as a sluggish bolt before anything else does.
steps.prose: Keep the oil film thin -- standing oil in an inertia receiver collects the next box of powder residue.
steps.caution: CAUTION: Use of Full or Improved Modified choke tubes is not recommended with steel shot.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Leave the choke tube installed when cleaning the bore to prevent residue from being deposited on the internal barrel threads.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — MAINTENANCE, p.17

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, forend, bolt handle and bolt group are off the stock/receiver and the magazine cap is accounted for. That is the whole routine strip the Model 3500 asks for, and every surface that fouls in normal use is now reachable. Deep Clean opens the bolt group itself -- firing pin, locking head, inertia spring -- and lifts the trigger group out of the receiver as a unit.
steps.prose: The trigger group comes out whole and goes no further than that outside a gunsmith's bench.
steps.quote: The shotgun is now completely stripped. All the parts that require routine maintenance and cleaning are disassembled.
steps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY (Continued), p.15

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin -- trap the pin first
deepSteps.action: Put a thumb over the rear of the bolt to hold the firing pin and its spring, then push the firing pin retaining pin out. The pin is under spring load until the moment it is free, and it will jump the length of a bench if it is not trapped. Work over a tray so a launched pin is a nuisance rather than a lost part.
deepSteps.quote: 7. While holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place, remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly (Fig. 18).
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY OF THE BOLT, step 7, p.14
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: The firing pin is under spring pressure.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin and spring out
deepSteps.action: Release your thumb slowly and let the spring push the firing pin clear, then lift both out together. Keep them as a pair; the manual insists the pin goes back with its spring, and a pin refitted without it will not reach the primer. Look at the tip while it is out -- a battered nose on a 3 1/2 inch gun is worth catching early.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Remove the firing pin and firing pin spring from the bolt (Fig. 19).
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY OF THE BOLT, step 8, p.14

deepSteps.title: Locking head pin, then the locking head
deepSteps.action: Push out the locking head pin and draw the locking head forward out of the bolt body. Those two lugs are what hold against 3 1/2 inch chamber pressure, so clean the carbon out from behind them and check the lug faces for battering. Note how the head sits: its shank groove has to line up with the hole in the bolt body when it goes back.
deepSteps.caution: 9. Remove the locking head pin from the bolt (Fig. 20).
deepSteps.quote: 10. Pull the locking head from the bolt body (Fig. 21).
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY OF THE BOLT, step 10, p.14

deepSteps.title: Inertia spring out of its seat
deepSteps.action: Tip the bolt and let the inertia spring drop into your palm. This is the operating system of the whole gun -- it sits between the locking head and the bolt body and stores the recoil energy that cycles the action. Clean it and its seat and look hard for a set or a cracked coil, because a tired spring on a supermagnum diet short-strokes with light loads and no amount of scrubbing elsewhere cures it.
deepSteps.quote: 11. Remove the inertia spring from its seat in the bolt, dropping it into the palm of your hand (Fig. 22).
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY (Continued), step 11, p.15

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard pin out, trigger group out
deepSteps.action: Drift the trigger guard pin out of the stock/receiver left to right with a properly-fitting punch. Then press and hold the bolt release with your left hand and pull the trigger guard assembly out of the receiver with your right -- the group will not clear its cut unless the bolt release is held down. It comes out as one piece and goes back the same way.
deepSteps.quote: 13. Press and hold the bolt release with the left hand and pull the trigger guard assembly out of the receiver with the right hand (Fig. 24).
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY (Continued), step 13, p.15

deepSteps.title: The trigger group is cleaned assembled -- it does not come apart
deepSteps.action: Wash fouling and debris off the trigger group with it still built up, dry it and oil it lightly. Stoeger stops the M3500 owner here: opening the group is a gunsmith job, not an owner job. Refit it as a unit with the hammer cocked so it seats properly in the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The caution is set around figure 24 in the printed layout of this page.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: Further dis- assembly of the Fig. 24 trigger group is not recommended, except by a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY (Continued), p.15
deepSteps.warn: Trigger group internals: qualified gunsmith only.

deepSteps.title: Bolt reassembly order is a safety item
deepSteps.action: Put the bolt back together in the published order, because where the inertia spring ends up decides whether the gun is safe. It has to sit between the locking head and the bolt body; assembled otherwise the M3500 can discharge as the bolt closes. Slide the locking head home with the bolt-body hole on the shank groove -- done right, the slanted surfaces on the head's stem are hidden.
deepSteps.prose: Then firing pin and spring, then the retaining pin to capture them.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: Always make sure that the inertia spring (or bolt recoil spring) is positioned between the locking head and the bolt itself, in order to avoid discharging the weapon when the bolt is closed.
deepSteps.cite: Stoeger Model 3500 Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — ASSEMBLY AFTER CLEANING, step 3, p.16
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: Improper assembly of the bolt group can cause accidental discharge resulting in serious injury or death.

cleaning.name: BORE, CHOKE & BARREL
tasks: Clean the bore with the choke still fitted so residue stays off the internal barrel threads
Remove the choke with the supplied wrench and clean tube and recess separately
Clean and lubricate the choke threads before refitting; the tube must sit flush, not proud of the muzzle
No Full or Improved Modified choke tube with steel shot

cleaning.name: BOLT GROUP
tasks: Strip the bolt: retaining pin, firing pin and spring, locking head pin, locking head, inertia spring
Clear carbon from both locking lugs and from the recesses behind them
Inspect the firing pin tip and the inertia spring for a set or cracked coil
Rebuild with the inertia spring between the locking head and the bolt body

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Wipe fouling and debris from the receiver
Oil the outside of the magazine tube, which guides the recoil spring
Clean the trigger group as an assembled unit -- do not open it

reassembly: Rebuild the bolt: inertia spring between locking head and bolt body; locking head with its shank groove on the bolt-body hole until the slanted surfaces vanish; locking head pin; firing pin with its spring; retaining pin.
Hold the carrier release pressed, insert the trigger group with the hammer cocked and its rear against the receiver, then drift the trigger guard pin back right to left until flush.
Fit the recoil spring over the magazine tube, mate the bolt to the action bar and seat it fully, slide the action bar into the receiver, then push the bolt handle home.
Refit the forend to the barrel ring, run the barrel/forend down the magazine tube and push until it clicks against metal and the forend meets the receiver.
Tighten the magazine cap firmly, and re-check it after the first few rounds -- it is what keeps the barrel fastened to the receiver.
fncheck: Gun empty: press the cartridge drop lever and pull the bolt fully back; it should lock open. Safety ON, press the bolt release to close the bolt, pull the trigger -- the hammer must NOT fall. Safety OFF so the red ring shows, pull and hold the trigger and the hammer should fall. Still holding the trigger, open the bolt, press the bolt release, let it close, then release the trigger and listen for the disconnector's click. Pull again and the hammer should fall.
